ky_bald_rock_fork_recreational_preserve_.blurb: A group of cliff lines tucked into a valley in the Red River Gorge area of Lee County, Kentucky. Nearly all of the climbing is sport, with a small amount of trad and almost no bouldering. Grades start around 5.6 and reach 5.14, but the weight sits squarely in the 5.10 to 5.12 range, with 5.11 the most common and a healthy number of 5.13s above it; moderates exist but are thin. Chocolate Factory is the largest crag, followed by the Motherlode, known for steep, demanding lines among the toughest in the gorge, and the Bear's Den. Expect a place built around hard, overhanging sport climbing rather than easy cragging.

nv_kraft_boulders.blurb: The busiest bouldering zone in Red Rock Canyon, on the Calico Basin side just outside Las Vegas, at roughly 3,700 feet and among the lowest-lying parts of the canyon. The rock is high-quality sandstone, and hundreds of problems are scattered over several clusters, including the West Cluster and the Cube Area. Grades run from V0 to V12, with the bulk between V1 and V5 and a thinner tail of hard problems, so it suits mixed groups. The boulders are mostly open to sun and wind, though the variety of blocks lets you hunt for shade or warmth, which makes it a favourite in winter. Trees and wildflowers soften the desert setting.

nc_rumbling_bald_bouldering.blurb: Gneiss boulders scattered through forest near Chimney Rock and Lake Lure in the southern mountains of North Carolina, at about 1,600 feet. All of it is bouldering, with problems from V0 up to V11 and a broad, even middle; the most popular lines fall roughly between V2 and V8. The West Side holds well over half of the problems, the East Side most of the rest, and the Central Boulders a small handful. The slope has a southern exposure, so the rock soaks up sun: midwinter is the prime time and it is a staple of the southern winter circuit, while summer is a poor fit because of the heat and abundant poison ivy.

nv_sandstone_quarry.blurb: A sport-climbing hub in Red Rock Canyon west of Las Vegas, set in open desert at about 4,300 feet. Sport routes make up most of the climbing, with a good dose of trad, a few top-ropes and a scattering of boulder problems. Grades centre on 5.10 to 5.12, with 5.11 the most common, a useful spread of easier lines from 5.7 to 5.9, and a few 5.13s and 5.14s at the top. Dozens of separate walls are spread across the zone, including the Parking Lot Area and the Wake-Up Wall. The sandstone is fragile when wet, so it pays to wait for dry ground after rain. Red Rock as a whole is said to climb best in late fall and early spring.

co_goose_creek_molly_gulch_campground.blurb: The heart of the "Inner Platte" in the South Platte, Colorado, at around 8,300 feet, with the largest collection of granite domes in the South Platte. Knobs, feldspar crystals and dikes give the granite good friction for face and slab climbing, with cracks on some formations. Trad is the biggest share, then sport, plus a few boulder problems and top-ropes. Grades run from easy fifth class to 5.13, with 5.10 the most common and a good supply of 5.7 to 5.9. Sheeprock is the largest zone, with long bolted face and slab lines on a tall, shaded north wall; Helen's Dome faces west and is sunny from midmorning on; Whiskey Rocks and Acid Rock add more. Granite is slick when wet, and midday summer shade is scarce.

wa_mazama.blurb: A sport-climbing destination along Highway 20 in Okanogan County, Washington, just east of Washington Pass at about 2,100 feet. Sport routes dominate, ranging from single pitches to long multi-pitch lines, with a good amount of bouldering and only a little trad and ice. Grades run from 5.6 to 5.13, centred on 5.9 to 5.11. The Fun Rocks are the largest zone and the local hub, mixing moderate routes with harder ones; the Matrix is a quieter alternative with closely bolted lines from 5.6 to 5.11, best on shoulder-season days or cooler summer ones; Goat Wall is the place for big multi-pitch climbs. Prospector Crags and Europa are nearby.
